{"context":"[ATLAS-SUB-001]
Subscription-4. An upgrade takes effect when the billing owner confirms it in the console, and the price difference for the remaining period is charged. The exact difference is shown on the payment screen before confirmation. A downgrade takes effect at the next renewal and does not refund the price difference for time that has already elapsed. To determine how a canceled renewal and a plan change interact, check the next billing details on the confirmation screen.

[ATLAS-FEAT-001]
Features-1. Organization SSO is available on Pro and is not included in Standard or Starter. IP allowlists are available on Standard and Pro. The features listed here apply to paid plans; the same features are not guaranteed during a free trial.","query":"Our team works exclusively through organization SSO. If we schedule a downgrade from Pro to Standard, will SSO disappear during the current paid period? Please also tell me whether SSO remains included after the next renewal."}

{"answer":"A downgrade takes effect at the next renewal, so scheduling it does not immediately turn the current paid Pro period into Standard. Once Standard takes effect at the next renewal, organization SSO is not included. Review your team's access methods before making the change.","citations":["ATLAS-SUB-001","ATLAS-FEAT-001"],"route":"answer","needs_human":false}

{"context":"[ATLAS-REF-001]\nRefund-1. A first purchase of a prepaid monthly subscription made at or after 2026-09-01 00:00:00 KST is eligible for a full-refund review if all three conditions are met: the request is within 14 days of payment, no paid production jobs have been run, and no paid credits have been used. Fourteen days means 14 x 24 hours, including the exact timestamp obtained by adding 14 days to the payment time. Meeting these conditions establishes eligibility to apply, not evidence of approval or a completed funds transfer.","query":"I bought a monthly subscription for the first time on September 20, 2026, and it's now the next day. I haven't run any production jobs, but I used some paid credits. Since I didn't run any jobs, do I meet the conditions to apply for a full refund?"}

{"answer":"All three conditions must be met. Even within the time limit and without any production jobs, using paid credits means you do not meet the standard conditions to apply for a full-refund review.","citations":["ATLAS-REF-001"],"route":"answer","needs_human":false}

{"context":"[ATLAS-REF-001]\nRefund-5. After receipt is acknowledged, the review target is three business days. Approved refunds are targeted to appear on the original payment method within five to seven business days. Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding Korean public holidays. Timing depends on approval and the payment provider's processing, so do not guarantee that funds will arrive on a specific calendar date. Without a receipt or approval record, do not claim that submission or processing is complete.","query":"I received acknowledgment of my refund request, but it hasn't been approved yet. Are the three business days and five to seven business days in the guidance the same period, or do they start at different points?"}

{"answer":"They refer to different stages and start at different points. The review target is three business days after receipt is acknowledged; the target for the refund to appear on the original payment method is five to seven business days after approval. If approval has not occurred, you cannot assume that the latter period has already started, and a final arrival date is not guaranteed.","citations":["ATLAS-REF-001"],"route":"answer","needs_human":false}

{"context":"[ATLAS-SLA-001]\nSLA-2. Monthly availability is calculated as (total minutes in the month - qualifying downtime minutes) / total minutes in the month x 100. Do not round before comparing against thresholds. Scheduled maintenance announced at least 48 hours in advance is excluded from qualifying downtime up to a combined 120 minutes per month; any excess is included. Maintenance announced less than 48 hours in advance is included in full. Customer configuration errors and failures in the customer's external network are excluded.","query":"Assume our office router failed, leaving us unable to connect for 40 minutes, and Atlas's qualifying downtime for that month was confirmed as zero minutes. Since users couldn't access the service, do those 40 minutes count toward the SLA?"}

{"answer":"If, as assumed, the issue was in the customer's internal network, those 40 minutes are excluded from qualifying downtime. With zero minutes of qualifying Atlas downtime, availability for this calculation is 100%. This explains the policy under your assumptions; it does not verify the actual cause.","citations":["ATLAS-SLA-001"],"route":"answer","needs_human":false}

{"context":"[ATLAS-SLA-001]\nSLA-3. Credits are 0% when monthly availability is at least 99.9%; 10% when it is at least 99.0% but below 99.9%; 25% when it is at least 95.0% but below 99.0%; and 50% when it is below 95.0%. The percentage applies to the affected service's base subscription fee for that month, not to usage-based charges. For an annual subscription, the monthly base amount is the actual prepaid annual subscription fee divided by 12. Total credits for one month are capped at 50% of that month's base amount.","query":"Someone asked me to multiply the entire annual prepaid amount by a one-month SLA rate of 50%. How should I explain the monthly base amount and monthly cap for annual customers?"}

{"answer":"For an annual subscription, the monthly base amount is the actual prepaid annual subscription fee divided by 12. Both the month's 50% rate and the total monthly cap apply to that monthly base, so you must not calculate one month's compensation as half the entire annual amount.","citations":["ATLAS-SLA-001"],"route":"answer","needs_human":false}
